answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent identity to a stake that is expensive to fake at scale: before it can transact, it must lock a deposit and build a history of attested work, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it cheating. Like a sparrow that must build a real nest before claiming a territory, a sybil farm cannot cheaply spin up thousands of identities, because each needs its own stake and record. An opal-grade reputation score, earned slowly from verified interactions, then gates access to higher-value tasks, keeping fake accounts out of the valuable parts of the economy.
